chunks: A group of scholars narrated from Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh, from Muhammad ibn Yaqub, who raised it to Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:

After the passing of my father, Imam Muhammad al-Hasan (peace be upon him), doubts overwhelmed me. A large amount of wealth had been deposited with my father, so he carried it and boarded a ship. I went with him to accompany him. He fell ill with a severe fever. He said to me: 'My son, take me back, take me back; this is death. And fear Allah regarding this wealth.' He confided his final will to me and died. I said to myself: 'My father did not ask me to do anything wrong. I will carry this wealth to Iraq and rent a house by the river, and I will not inform anyone. If something becomes clear to me, as clear as it was during the days of my father, Imam Muhammad (peace be upon him), I will send it [to the Imam]; otherwise, I will give it in charity.' I arrived in Iraq and rented a house by the river. I remained there for a few days when suddenly a messenger came to me with a note saying: 'O Muhammad, you have with you such and such [amounts] in such and such parcels,' recounting all the wealth with me of which I had no knowledge. I handed the wealth to the messenger. I remained there for a few more days and received no attention, which made me sad. Then a message came to me: 'We have appointed you in the position of your father, so thank Allah.'

key_terms.أَقَمْنَاكَ مَقَامَ أَبِيكَ: We have appointed you in the position of your father

ai.seo_question: How did Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar become a representative of the Imam during the Minor Occultation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the transition from the Major to the Minor Occultation, highlighting the continuity of divine authority through the *Na'ib al-Khas* (special deputy). The narrator’s secret retention of Khums and the subsequent miraculous confirmation of its exact location by the Imam’s messenger underscore the concept of *Ismah* (infallibility) and divine oversight during the period of concealment. It serves as a foundational proof for the legitimacy of the deputies' authority to collect and manage religious funds without public scrutiny.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 239 - A group of scholars has narrated from Abul Qasim Ja’far bin Muhammad Quluwayh from Muhammad bin Yaqub directly from Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Mahziyar that he said:

After the martyrdom of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) doubts overwhelmed me, especially about who would be the Imam after him. This was while a huge amount of Khums had been deposited with my father; so he carried them and boarded a ship. I went with him to accompany him. He got a very severe fever and said to me, “My son, take me back, take me back. This is death. And fear Allah in this Khums.” He confided his final will to me and died. I said to myself that my father had not asked me to do anything wrong. I will carry these goods to Iraq and will rent a house there and will not inform anyone. If things became clear to me like their clarity during the days of Imam Hasan Askari (a.s), I will hand the goods over, or else, distribute them as alms. I went to Iraq and rented a house by the river. I had remained there but a few days that a messenger brought a letter to me saying: O Muhammad, you have brought this and this in such and such parcels; recounting all of the goods that were with me of which I did not know myself. I gave them to the messenger. I remained there a few more days and was not given any attention, which made me rather sad. Then a letter came, “We have appointed you in the position of your father, so thank Allah.”
